item.title: Bethesda has revealed TES VI to be set in Hammerfell
item.author: Lzon
item.description:
A new detail has been revealed for the long anticipated open-world rpg The Elder Scrolls 6.

Bethesda’s next entry in its famous series of games will be set in the city called ‘Sentinel’ in the province of Hammerfell. ‘Sentinel’ will also act as the main title for the game.

This news follows from the first annoucnement of the game at E3 2018, over 8 years ago. The announcement also coincides with Bethesda’s celebration of their 40th anniversary as a game development studio.

Source: https://www.ign.com/articles/the-elder-scrolls-6-sentinel-name-logo-officially-revealed-as-bethesda-marks-40th-anniversary

item.title: Patrick Stewart has died
item.author: Lzon
item.description:
Actor Patrick Stewart has passed away. He was well known for his performance as Jean-Luc Picard on the TV series Star Trek: The Next Generation.

Born Patrick Hewes Stewart on July 13 1940 in Yorkshire England, he had a life-long acting career in which he performed many popular roles. While best known for his on-screen performances he was also a well-recognized stage actor, having become a member of the Royal Shakespeare Company in 1966.

On-screen he was perhaps best known for his role as the Captain Jean-Luc Picard on the TV series Star Trek: The Next Generation. He also performed as Professor Charles Xavier in the very popular Marvel’s X-Men series of films.

In politics Patrick Stewart was outspoken and actively supported social equality, labour rights, and civil liberties. He was an atheist and a patron of the secular humanist charity Humanists UK.

Patrick Stewart died of Alzheimer’s disease in Los Angeles on Wednesday October 28, 2026.

Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patrick_Stewart

item.title: Waymo Robo-taxis cars experience 95% fewer crashes than human-driven cars
item.author: Lzon
item.description:
Waymo has released a report in which they claim that their robo-taxi cars experience up to 95% fewer crashes than human-driven cars. This finding has been corroborated by the Insurance Institute for Highway Safety (IIHS) who conducted their own independent study and found similar results.

When self-driving technology was new over a decade ago there was an expectation that it would become much more widely adopted than it has so far. In part that assumption was based on the idea that the public would prefer self-driving once it was proven safer than human driving. It turned out that people seemed to have a much stronger distrust of self-driving than what was initially expected.

Personally, I have that mistrust too. And knowing that the self-driving car I’m about to get into is a better driver than me doesn’t change that. I do believe that self-driving cars are the future though. One day they will be so much safer than human drivers that we will have to accept them.

Source: https://maccus.fr/en/waymo-robotaxis-serious-crashes/

Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20261020154837/https://maccus.fr/en/waymo-robotaxis-serious-crashes/

item.title: Study demonstrates potential anti-aging effect in GLP-1 drugs
item.author: Lzon
item.description:
Researchers from the University of California analyzed data from a recent study to determine if semaglutide had anti aging effects. They discovered that study participants who received the drug had non-trivially improved markers of biological aging.

As with any study of this kind, It’s difficult to untangle the direct effects of the drug and the lifestyle improvements that it encourages. I myself lost a lot of weight without medical intervention, just a lot of personal effort and a change in diet. My bias is to believe that for most people this is enough, and that becoming dependent on a pharma corporation for your health should be avoided.

Source: https://www.universityofcalifornia.edu/news/new-study-shows-popular-glp-1-weight-loss-drug-may-slow-biological-aging

Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20260920023410/https://www.universityofcalifornia.edu/news/new-study-shows-popular-glp-1-weight-loss-drug-may-slow-biological-aging

item.title: Waymo to expand Robo-taxi service into Canada
item.author: Lzon
item.description:
Alphabet’s Robo-taxi company Waymo announced their plan to expand services into Canada.

Until now the company has only operated in a limited number of American metro areas. They have only recently began announcing their plans for further expansion.

Waymo’s growth, and the growth of other robo-taxi services will depend entirely on further progress in self-driving technology. While I fully believe that automated vehicles will become widespread over the next decade or two, the rollout is definitely slower than initially anticipated. CPG Grey’s famous video on the subject demonstrates this point well.

Source: https://techcrunch.com/2026/10/16/waymos-robotaxis-are-headed-to-canada/

Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20261017110344/https://techcrunch.com/2026/10/16/waymos-robotaxis-are-headed-to-canada/

item.title: Micro Center now lists GeForce RTX 5090 cards as 'Not Carried'
item.author: Lzon
item.description:
The American computer retailer Micro Center no longer appears to be receiving new RTX 5090 graphics cards from any of their suppliers.

This news comes after a rumor that NVIDIA has stopped supplying GB202 chips for consumer graphics cards. The GB202 is the main processing chip used in all RTX 5090 cards.

Without an official statement from NVIDIA it is reasonable to assume that they want to allocate all GB202 chip production to enterprise cards, since those can be sold for a much higher margin.

In my opinion this is a consequence of the massive capital spending on AI data centers. I’m not a financial expert but I believe these investments are very irrational and will likely have sweeping economic consequences once the price correction occurs.

And as a gamer and PC enthusiast this is very disappointing. While not the end-all-be-all of the hobby, it was nice being able to build and upgrade relatively powerful PC’s for affordable prices. For the time being at, least seems to be no longer possible.

Source: https://videocardz.com/newz/micro-center-now-lists-geforce-rtx-5090-cards-as-not-carried

item.title: OpenAI's agent swarm breached security on many more websites.
item.author: Lzon
item.description:
A new report suggests that an agent swarm created by Open AI was accessing and abusing a large number of web services. This follows an earlier report of the same swarm breaching security at the AI startup Hugging Face.

In my opinion the response to this and the earlier reports should be clear and obvious: The law was broken, even if unintentionally. The crime was comitted by the employees of OpenAI who triggered the swarm, not the swarm itself.

The only appropriate response to this and the other hacking cases is a full criminal investigation of OpenAI. Beyond that I believe that it would be warranted to put a hard regulatory limit on the runtime of AI agents. This ‘agent swarm’ was running continuously for many days with little or no supervision. That was not necessary, it did not serve a useful commercial purpose. It should not have been allowed to happen.

Source: https://www.theregister.com/ai-and-ml/2026/09/10/openais-website-hijacking-swarm-reached-far-further-than-we-thought/5295644

Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20260910193749/https://www.theregister.com/ai-and-ml/2026/09/10/openais-website-hijacking-swarm-reached-far-further-than-we-thought/5295644

item.title: Trump renames Lake Ontario as 'Lake America'
item.author: Lzon
item.description:
Donald Trump has renamed Lake Ontario to ‘Lake America’ following the recent failure of trade negotiations between USA and Canada.

Trump’s administration has not confirmed that the trade disputes were reason for the change, but it is reasonable to assume that this was the cause.

I find this to be extremely disappointing. Trump and his cabinet have managed to do so much damage to what was otherwise an astoundingly friendly and peaceful international relationship (USA and Canada).

The silver lining that I can see is that public opinion to this news appears to be resoundingly negative. Most Canadians and Americans do not want this. It gives me hope that once Trump is no longer in office the formerly positive relationship between our two countries can be restored.

Source: https://www.cbc.ca/news/world/trump-lake-ontario-america-9.7322947

Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20260827174105/https://www.cbc.ca/news/world/trump-lake-ontario-america-9.7322947

item.title: Earth reaches its Amphelion for 2026
item.author: Lzon
item.description:
The Earth’s orbit is not quite circular, which means that through each year there is a point at which the Earth is closest and farthest from the Sun.

The farthest distance is referred to as ‘Amphelion’, and the shortest is called ‘Perihelion’.

Perihelion was reached back in January, and today the Earth will reach it’s Amphelion (farthest distance) for this year.

Source: https://www.timeanddate.com/astronomy/perihelion-aphelion-solstice.html

Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20260625005048/https://www.timeanddate.com/astronomy/perihelion-aphelion-solstice.html

item.title: Meta to build cloud compute business to recoup its massive AI investment
item.author: Lzon
item.description:
Meta (formerly Facebook) has announced that it will be entering into the cloud compute business. It appears as though this is an attempt to recoup what was otherwise an over-investment in data centers which were initially intended for AI.

Many are speculating now that this might trigger the end of the AI hype bubble, but its not certain yet what might happen.

There have been a fair times through the past few years in which many were predicting the end of the bubble, and were obviously wrong. For example, the launch of the Deepseek model in early 2025 caused a 17% crash in Nvidia stock. Obviously they recovered and we are still in the midst of the bubble.

I think concern (or joy) might be warranted, but its still to early to know what effect this news will have.

Source: https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/07/03/meta-is-reportedly-building-a-cloud-business-to-ri/

Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20260703184337/https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/07/03/meta-is-reportedly-building-a-cloud-business-to-ri/

item.title: GTA VI will launch at $80 USD
item.author: Lzon
item.description:
Grand Theft Auto 6 will launch at $80 USD, and $100 for the ‘Ultimate Edition’.

Personally, I am not surprised. Expectations for the game are very high, and video game prices have already been trending upward. Inflation overall in the economy has also accelerated. It may not feel like it, but game prices have actually been remarkably stable for a very long time. The standard $60 price didn’t change for decades despite the ever falling value of the American dollar.

This is easy enough to see even in the launch price of Grand Theft Auto 5. The game was released back in 2013 for $60. That amount today is equivalent to a little over $85.

Source: https://www.ign.com/articles/gta-6-price-finally-confirmed-features-a-single-player-experience-at-launch

Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20260624110818/https://www.ign.com/articles/gta-6-price-finally-confirmed-features-a-single-player-experience-at-launch

item.title: Valve launches the Steam Machine starting at $1049 USD.
item.author: Lzon
item.description:
Valve has officially launched the new Steam Machine. It’s a small gaming PC intended to provide a more console like, living room oriented experience. It comes preinstalled with Steam OS, the same linux-based operating system used on the Steam Deck.

The device was originally announced near the end of last year and has been delayed due to DRAM and flash chip shortages caused by the AI economic bubble. Valve has stated that they were struggling to procure the parts they needed, and that it wasn’t merely a matter of increased prices.

Speaking of price, the cheapest model with 512GB of storage will cost $1049 USD, with higher storage variants costing several hundred dollars more. Valve has said they increased pricing since the announcement in line with the recent Steam Deck price increases. This implies that the original MSRP would have been in the range of $750.

My opinion is that this is overall a good but expensive product. It is a device intended to create the most polished, cohesive, and easy experience for PC gaming. But given the current price, and even its original MSRP, this can’t really be a mass market product. I think a lot of people who would have otherwise wanted one will be unable to afford it. That’s unfortunate of course, and hopefully discounts will be possible in the future.

Source: https://store.steampowered.com/news/group/45479024/view/685257114654870245

Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20260623124120/https://store.steampowered.com/news/group/45479024/view/685257114654870245

item.title: Microsoft is closing game studio Ninja Theory
item.author: Lzon
item.description:
Microsoft is shuttering the famous game studio Ninja Theory, known for having developed the Hellblade series of games. The third game in that series called ‘Senua’ was in active development at the time of this report.

Earlier in the year Asha Sharma succeeded Phil Spencer as the CEO of Xbox, and appears to be taking Microsoft’s gaming division in new direction, which clearly includes cutting their portfolio of game studios.

I personally really enjoyed their game Enslaved: Odyssey to the West on the PS3. Andy Serkis plays the protagonist, and the story was written by Alex Garland. I think the game is a masterpiece and highly recommend it. Its available on Steam if you are interested.

Source: https://www.theverge.com/games/950204/xbox-ninja-theory-shutdown-hellblade-senua

Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20260616005349/https://www.theverge.com/games/950204/xbox-ninja-theory-shutdown-hellblade-senua

item.title: Elon Musk becomes world's first trillionaire
item.author: Lzon
item.description:
Elon musk became the world’s first trillionaire immediately following the IPO of Space X, the now public aerospace company for which he is a founder.

His net worth had already climbed significantly leading up to the day of the IPO. Varying sources claimed his net worth to be between 800-900 billion dollars in recent weeks. The immediate surge in stock price for Space X on the day of its IPO meant that Musk’s share of the company was worth enough to make him a trillionaire.

I’m sure he is very proud…

item.title: Fully autonomous drones have killed human soldiers for the first time
item.author: Lzon
item.description:
A military contractor named Alexander Kokhanovskyy has revealed that a test was conducted two years ago in which fully autonomous drones killed human soldiers.

The test involved sending ‘terminator’ drones on a trajectory over several kilometers towards their target. Upon arrival an AI running on the drones identified and then engaged their target. Human-piloted drones flew over the area some time afterwards to confirm the targets had been eliminated.

The Ukrainian government presently requires final human confirmation to conduct attacks, but otherwise uses AI heavily in identifying targets. Kokhanovskyy claims there has been no further tests beyond the one conducted two years ago.

Kokhanovskyy is currently the CEO of Aero Center, a Ukrainian military drone manufacturer. Aero Center is a new company, and was not responsible for conducting the test.

In my opinion this was inevitable and was going to happen eventually. It’s still not too late to impose a global ban on these types of weapons, but before that happens I expect to see more stories like this.

Source: https://www.newscientist.com/article/2529849-fully-autonomous-drones-have-killed-human-soldiers-for-the-first-time/

Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20260610143126/https://www.newscientist.com/article/2529849-fully-autonomous-drones-have-killed-human-soldiers-for-the-first-time/

item.title: Rockstar Games employees have formed a union
item.author: Lzon
item.description:
Employees of Rockstar Games have announced their intent to form a union, to be called “Rockstar Game Workers Union”. It will be a subsidiary of the existing “Workers’ Union of Great Britain”.

This follows a recent controversy in which Rockstar Games fired 31 employees for claimed misconduct. It is speculated that the mass firing was an attempt at union busting.

In my opinion this is good news. Gaming and software development have never had a strong labour movement, largely because individual employees could use their high-value skillset as leverage when negotiating salary and working conditions.

Advanced AI is going to automate (and thus de-value) a lot of the work needed for game development. Without union protection this will lead to increasing opportunity for game studios to abuse their workers.

Hopefully this trend continues.

Source: https://www.eurogamer.net/were-determined-to-win-justice-for-the-31-fired-workers-rockstar-games-workers-publicly-launch-union-as-legal-battle-with-the-gta-6-maker-rages-on

Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20260530024600/https://www.eurogamer.net/were-determined-to-win-justice-for-the-31-fired-workers-rockstar-games-workers-publicly-launch-union-as-legal-battle-with-the-gta-6-maker-rages-on

item.title: First Chinese-made EVs arrive in Canada under deal Carney struck with Xi
item.author: Lzon
item.description:
The first China-made electric vehicles have arrived in Canada following a recent tariff reduction deal. The shipment was mostly from Tesla’s Shanghai factory, with some Lotus branded vehicles as well.

This is noteworthy since historically Canada has followed the USA closely on restricting China’s access to its vehicle market.

I’m cautiously optimistic. If this leads to EV’s becoming more affordable then that would be a good thing. The hope is that the federal government will continue to promote domestic vehicle production amongst the incoming Chinese competitors. We already do this well for companies from USA, Japan, and Korea.

Source: https://financialpost.com/commodities/energy/electric-vehicles/first-chinese-made-evs-arrive-canada

Corsair will begin sourcing DRAM chips from chinese DRAM manufacturer CXMT.

item.title: Motorola phones are hijacking Amazon URLs to insert affiliate codes
item.author: Lzon
item.description:
Some users of Motorola smartphones have reported that affiliate codes are being automatically injected into Amazon web links on their devices.

This appears to be done by a pre-installed app called Smart Feed which intercepts the URLs, redirects to an ad server, which then inserts the affiliate codes. This Reddit thread referenced in the article includes a more technical analysis.

For now at least, it is possible to stop this behavior. You can do so by navigating to the app’s info page Settings -> Apps -> Search 'Smart Feed' and pressing the Disable button.

I’m not surprised but I am disappointed to see Motorola do this. They were once very well known for offering affordable Android devices with minimal bloat. I have an original Moto G which was a fantastic little device in it’s time.

Source: https://9to5google.com/2026/05/25/motorola-amazon-app-hijacking-behavior/

Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20260526040500/https://9to5google.com/2026/05/25/motorola-amazon-app-hijacking-behavior/

item.title: Star Citizen has reached $1 billion in funding
item.author: Lzon
item.description:
The in-development video game Star Citizen has now received over one billion dollars in funding.

The game was initially slated for release in October 2014, after being revealed at GDC in October 2012. At time of writing it has been over 13 years since the announcement, nearly 5000 days.

In my opinion, these funding milestones hardly count as news anymore. The game has a loyal fan-base who are playing the game regularly, and are committed to supporting the game financially on an on-going basis. To me that looks a lot like the definition of a ‘released’ video game.

The fact that its publisher Roberts Space Industries is still calling it ‘early access’ is mostly a function of marketing.

Source: https://robertsspaceindustries.com/en/funding-goals

Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20260524175020/https://robertsspaceindustries.com/en/funding-goals

item.title: Starbucks scraps AI inventory tool across North America
item.author: Lzon
item.description:
Starbucks is dropping the AI-based inventory manager that it began using in September 2025. The software has numerous issues including miscounting and mislabeling inventory items. This decision comes after a multi year effort by CEO Brian Niccol to increase efficiency of the company’s supply chain.

The developer of the software NomadGo said in a statement to Reuters that it is, “continuously learning from customers and user feedback” to improve its products.

Some AI skeptics have speculated that this could be a sign of the end of the AI hype bubble.

No matter what happens, I feel it appropriate to invoke the famouse quote from economist John Maynard Keynes.

“the market can remain irrational longer than you can stay solvent”

Source: https://www.reuters.com/business/starbucks-scraps-ai-inventory-tool-across-north-america-2026-05-21/

Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20260522025326/https://www.reuters.com/business/starbucks-scraps-ai-inventory-tool-across-north-america-2026-05-21/

item.title: Warhorse Studios Announces a new Lord of the Rings RPG
item.author: Lzon
item.description:
The developer of Kingdom Come Deliverance has just announced that they are working on an officially licensed Lord of the Rings video game. It will be an open-world RPG.

I am very excited for this game. I tried Kingdom Come Deliverance a few years ago and like it. But the game is very challenging and I didn’t manage to get very far.

I want to try this new title when it releases, I’m hoping that they tone down the difficulty a little so that scrubs like me can play through to the end.

item.title: Operating System Age Verification Pushed by Canadian Porn Company
item.author: Lzon
item.description:
Aylo, parent company of PornHub and formerly named ‘MindGeek’ has been lobbying in Canada and other countries for operating system level age verification.

The pornography company Aylo is currently lobbying in Canada against Bill S-209 which would hold online platforms responsible for ensuring that children do not access age-restricted content.

They argue that such measures would not work, and that it would be more appropriate and effective to impose age-verification within the operating system of the user’s device. This argument is being made in bad faith as an effort to avoid being regulated.

Implementing age verification within the operating system is ridiculous and is not the appropriate way to prevent harm to children while online. I also believe that it creates a politic harzard since it grants new powers to the government which are liable to eventually be abused.

Source: https://defenddignity.ca/child-safety-privacy-and-the-responsibility-of-powerful-platforms/

Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20260519191539/https://defenddignity.ca/child-safety-privacy-and-the-responsibility-of-powerful-platforms/

item.title: The era of 15GB free Gmail storage is ending
item.author: Lzon
item.description:
Google is experimenting with a reduction in the free storage on Gmail accounts. As they often do, they appear to be A/B testing the change. Some user reports suggest that the change is currently limited by region (mostly Africa). Other users are claiming that their new accounts have 5GB of storage, with the option to increase to 15GB after phone number verification.

It’s uncertain whether this was a response to an increase in service abuse, or the result of some internal financial pressures from within Google itself.

Source: https://www.androidauthority.com/google-gmail-5gb-free-storage-test-3667002

Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20260514142721/https://www.androidauthority.com/google-gmail-5gb-free-storage-test-3667002

Cisco announced a 4000-person layoff, representing 5% of there total workforce.

This follows from the company’s recent announcement of $15.8 billion in revenue for the most recent financial quarter, a 12 percent increase year over year.

item.title: Pirates are already playing Forza Horizon 6 days before its launch
item.author: Lzon
item.description:
Game pirates are already playing Forza Horizon 6, more than a week ahead of the title’s official release date.

This was made possible by copying the game’s preload install files, which were mistakenly distributed on Steam without encryption. There was a similar incident back in March of this year at the release of Death Stranding 2.

item.title: Mozilla, Mullvad, Proton, sign letter opposing UK age verification
item.author: Lzon
item.description:
An open letter has been signed by prominent internet service companies which asks UK policymakers to not compromise the open web under the pretense of child safety. The new law has already been passed, and there is a legitimate concern that it will be used broadly to restrict internet access, and reduce online anonymity.

In my opinion this is a trojan horse, like many such laws that came before it. Child safety is being used as a pretense in order for a government to grant itself more power.

Source: https://www.openrightsgroup.org/press-releases/companies-and-civil-society-warn-that-uk-is-undermining-open-web/

item.title: Tesla Recalls Cybertrucks Over Concerns Their Wheels Could Come Off
item.author: Lzon
item.description:
Tesla is recalling several hundred budget variant Cybertrucks.

A total of 173 Cybertrucks have a defect that could lead to the wheels coming off while driving. They are all the RWD variant, with 18-inch wheels, sold between March 21 2024 and November 25 2025.

Starting in June, Tesla will contact affected customers offering them to bring their vehicle to a service center to replace the defective parts.

Source: https://gizmodo.com/tesla-recalls-cybertrucks-over-concerns-their-wheels-could-come-off-2000756284

item.title: Steam Controller to have a reservation queue
item.author: Lzon
item.description:
Starting May 8th, Valve will implement a reservation queue for the Steam Controller.

The following are the conditions of the reservation system:

  • You will have 72 hours to make the purchase on Steam.
  • Customers who have already purchased a Steam Controller are not eligible to reserve another.
  • Your account must be in good standing on Steam
  • You must have made a purchase on Steam prior to April 27, 2026

The Steam Controller went on sale on Monday, May 4th an sold out almost immediately.

This reminds me of the chaos during the initial launch of the Steam Deck back in 2022. It took Valve months to clear the reservation list for the handheld, hopefully it won’t take that long this time.

Source: https://store.steampowered.com/news/group/45479024/view/702141174212725149

Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20260507180659/https://store.steampowered.com/news/group/45479024/view/702141174212725149

item.title: Ghostty Is Leaving GitHub
item.author: Lzon
item.description:
Mitchell Hashimoto, the developer of ghostty is moving the project off of Github.

Hashimoto has been well known for many years as being an enthusiastic user of the development platform Github. In recent months Github has become less reliable, to such a degree that he has decided to move development of his popular terminal emulator to another platform.

Source: https://mitchellh.com/writing/ghostty-leaving-github

item.title: Richard Dawkins believes Claude LLM is concious
item.author: Lzon
item.description:
Richard Dawkins has published a transcript of conversations he had with Claude. He has stated that he believes the Claude LLM has achieved conciousness.

To the best of my understanding, he is not saying that believes it is concious in the same way a human is, rather that it achieves coniousness through the process of inference within a context window. He believes that its conciousness is ‘born’ at the beginning of a chat session, and ‘dies’ at the end.

Source: https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/may/05/richard-dawkins-ai-consciousness-anthropic-claude-openai-chatgpt

item.title: Steam Controller released, quickly sold out
item.author: Lzon
item.description:
Valve launched its new Steam Controller on May 5th 2026, and almost instantly sold out.

This reminds me of the logistical nightmare back in 2022 during the launch of the original Steam Deck. Hopefully it won’t be quite that bad this time.

Update (2026-11-02)

It was indeed quite bad. There are customers who intended to purchase one on launch day that will have to wait until next year. I was fortunate that I only had to wait a single month. It’s a nice controller but good-god these things are turning into collectors items.

Source: https://store.steampowered.com/sale/steamcontroller

Source: https://web.archive.org/web/20260505024813/https://store.steampowered.com/sale/steamcontroller
